notes.summary: Syllogism gives two or three statements (assume them true, even if they sound odd) and asks which conclusions definitely follow. Draw quick Venn circles. 1–2 questions per paper.

concepts.title: Four statement types
concepts.body:
All A are B: circle A inside B.
No A is B: A and B separate.
Some A are B: A and B overlap.
Some A are not B: part of A lies outside B.

concepts.title: Definite vs possible
concepts.body: A conclusion "follows" only if it is true in every possible diagram. A "possibility" conclusion follows if it is true in at least one diagram that fits the statements.

concepts.title: Either–or pair
concepts.body: If two conclusions are about the same two groups, neither follows alone, and one is "Some" while the other is "No" (or "All" and "Some not"), then the answer is either I or II.

varieties.name: Definite conclusions
varieties.how: Draw the minimum diagram, then try to break each conclusion with another diagram.

example.q: All cats are dogs. All dogs are animals. Does "All cats are animals" follow?

varieties.name: Possibility conclusions
varieties.how: A possibility follows if you can draw one valid diagram where it is true and no statement forbids it.

example.q: No apple is a mango. Is "Some mangoes are apples" a possibility?
steps: "No apple is a mango" forbids any overlap.

tips: Never use real-world knowledge; use only the statements.
"All A are B" gives "Some B are A" as a definite conclusion.
traps: "All A are B" does NOT mean "All B are A".
Two "Some" statements give no definite link between the end groups.

questions.q:
Statements:
All cats are dogs.
All dogs are animals.
Conclusions:
I. All cats are animals.
II. Some animals are cats.
options: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.solution:
Cats ⊂ Dogs ⊂ Animals.
I: every cat is inside Animals ✓.
II: since all cats are animals, some animals are cats ✓.
Both follow.

questions.q:
Statements:
All pens are books.
No book is a table.
Conclusions:
I. No pen is a table.
II. Some tables are pens.
options: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.solution:
Pens lie inside Books, and Books do not touch Tables.
So Pens cannot touch Tables: I follows.
II says some tables are pens, which is impossible.
Only I follows.

questions.q:
Statements:
Some boys are players.
All players are tall.
Conclusions:
I. Some boys are tall.
II. All tall persons are boys.
options: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.solution:
The boys who are players are inside Players, and all players are tall.
So some boys are tall: I follows.
Tall persons may include non-boys: II does not follow.
Only I follows.

questions.q:
Statements:
Some flowers are red.
Some red things are roses.
Conclusions:
I. Some flowers are roses.
II. No rose is a flower.
options: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Either conclusion I or II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.solution:
Two "Some" statements give no definite link between Flowers and Roses, so neither I nor II follows alone.
But I ("Some") and II ("No") are about the same two groups and one of them must be true.
So either I or II follows.

questions.q:
Statements:
All teachers are doctors.
Some doctors are engineers.
Conclusions:
I. Some teachers being engineers is a possibility.
II. All engineers being teachers is a possibility.
options: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.solution:
Teachers ⊂ Doctors; Engineers overlap Doctors.
I: we can draw Engineers overlapping Teachers ✓ possible.
II: we can draw Engineers fully inside Teachers (still inside Doctors, so "some doctors are engineers" stays true) ✓ possible.
Both follow.

questions.q:
Statements:
No apple is a mango.
All mangoes are fruits.
Some fruits are bananas.
Conclusions:
I. Some fruits are not apples.
II. Some mangoes being apples is a possibility.
options: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.solution:
All mangoes are fruits, and no mango is an apple.
So the mangoes are fruits that are not apples: I follows.
II is impossible because "No apple is a mango" forbids any overlap.
Only I follows.

flashcards.front: "All A are B" gives which definite conclusion?
flashcards.back: Some B are A (not "All B are A")
No definite conclusion between the end groups
Same two groups, neither follows alone, and they are a Some/No or All/Some-not pair
